question: Which among the following states has the lowest poverty ratio as per the Multidimensional Poverty Index (2021) of the NITI Aayog?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kerala has the lowest poverty ratio in India as per the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) report by NITI Aayog in 2021.
 
• The state recorded a poverty ratio of only 0.71%, the lowest among all Indian states.
 
• This low poverty ratio is attributed to Kerala's robust social welfare schemes and high human development indicators.
 
• Kerala has consistently performed well in areas such as health, education, and standard of living, contributing to its low poverty levels.
 
• The state's effective implementation of public policies and high literacy rates are key factors in reducing poverty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**

 
 
• MPI is an international measure of acute multidimensional poverty covering over 100 developing countries.
 
• It identifies multiple deprivations at the household and individual level in health, education, and standard of living.
 
• Developed by the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• NITI Aayog's MPI report is an important tool for formulating poverty alleviation policies in India.
 
 
 
• **Kerala's Social Welfare Programs**
 
 
• Kerala has numerous social security schemes like the Kudumbashree program aimed at women empowerment and poverty eradication.
 
• The state offers comprehensive healthcare services through its primary health centers and the Aardram Mission.
 
• High literacy rates are maintained through initiatives such as the Akshara Keralam project focusing on adult education.
 
• The Public Distribution System (PDS) in Kerala ensures food security for its citizens.
 
 
 
• **Human Development Index (HDI)**
 
 
• HDI is a composite index measuring average achievement in three basic aspects of human development: health, education, and income.
 
• Kerala has consistently scored high on HDI due to its effective social policies.
 
• It provides insights into long-term progress in various dimensions of human development.
 
 
 
• **Economic Indicators in Kerala**
 
 
• Kerala's economy is driven by sectors such as tourism, remittances from the diaspora, and agriculture.
 
• The state has a relatively high per capita income compared to other Indian states.
 
• Investments in education and health have resulted in a skilled and healthy workforce.
